newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to launch securities loaning program Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to launch securities loaning program Jan 10.

text.p: Mexico on Friday will launch a program of securities loaning that is aimed at deepening liquidity in the markets and encouraging short-selling, the securities deposit institute Indeval said on Thursday.
It said the program, which will be run electronically via a system known as Valpre, will include stocks, Cetes, Bondes, ajustabonos, bank acceptances and other interest-bearing paper.

In a statement, Indeval said the Valpre system would allow banks, brokerages and individuals to put in bids to acquire or offer securities on loan, establish and administer the necessary guarantees and consult price movements.

It said any investor would only be allowed to rent a maximum five percent of the amount of an issue in circulation, and that no more than 15 percent of an issue in circulation could be loaned to investors as a whole.

It said there were two types of loaning, standard and automatic. The first involves renting with a fixed maturity date. If the borrower of the security returns it ahead of time, he must pay a surcharge on the interest on the loan.

In the automatic version, if the borrower does not have enough securities on the day of maturity to return them to the lender, he must accept that Indeval provides the securities for him, and charges extra.
